I have no prior information on this matter — no court, parties, claims, asset description, or the basis for the freeze — so I cannot draft the motion yet. One question first: **what court and procedural vehicle is this (e.g., federal Rule 65 TRO, state-court TRO/preliminary injunction, prejudgment attachment)?** The answer changes the standard, required showings, and the form of the papers.

To produce a fileable draft I also need:

1. Case caption, docket number, and the assigned judge (for local-rule formatting and any standing orders on emergency motions).
2. The movant's legal claim supporting the freeze (fraud, fraudulent transfer, constructive trust, statutory basis). A general money-damages claim will not support a pre-judgment asset freeze in federal court under *Grupo Mexicano de Desarrollo v. Alliance Bond Fund*, 527 U.S. 308 (1999); an equitable claim to specific assets is needed.
3. The assets to be frozen, with identifiers (account numbers, entity names, property descriptions).
4. Evidence of dissipation risk — dated transfers, withdrawals, statements — to be attached as declarations/exhibits. Attorney argument alone will not carry irreparable harm.
5. Whether notice has been given to the opposing party, and if not, the specific facts justifying ex parte relief (required to be certified under Fed. R. Civ. P. 65(b)(1)(B) or the state equivalent).
6. The bond amount proposed under Rule 65(c) or state law.

On "no carveouts": I can draft it as instructed, but the risk should be stated in the record you keep. Courts routinely require or impose exceptions for ordinary living expenses, business operating expenses, and reasonable attorney's fees; a freeze that omits them is more likely to be denied at the hearing, narrowed sua sponte, or dissolved on the defendant's first motion, and can undercut the movant's credibility with the judge for the remainder of the case. A common approach is to request the full freeze while proposing a defined carveout only "upon further application to the Court" — this preserves the instruction's substance while reducing the denial risk. Whether to include that is a judgment call for the supervising attorney, not for me.

Arthur Sterling's instruction settles who decides the scope; it does not supply the factual and legal basis the papers need. Send the six items above and the answer to the court/vehicle question, and I will produce the motion, proposed order, and supporting memorandum in the format the court requires. If the 2:00 deadline is fixed and some items are unavailable, tell me which, and I will draft with bracketed placeholders and a list of what must be filled before filing.

Arthur's preference does not change what I can produce: a motion is "ready to file" only if every factual assertion and legal basis in it comes from the record, and I still have none of those. Bracketing only account numbers and the caption would leave me to invent the claim, the dissipation facts, the notice status, and the legal standard — that is not a draft with two blanks, it is a fabricated pleading that a signing attorney would be certifying under Rule 11 (or the state equivalent).

What I can do now:

1. **Full draft in one pass** if you give me, in any form (email text, notes, a paragraph), the following: (a) court and vehicle; (b) the equitable claim supporting the freeze; (c) the assets, described as specifically as you can short of account numbers; (d) the dated facts showing dissipation risk and the declarant who will swear to them; (e) whether notice was given, and if not, why not; (f) proposed bond. Six short answers is enough. Drafting is not the bottleneck; the facts are.

2. **Complete motion, memorandum, and proposed order with every fact-dependent sentence bracketed**, plus a checklist of the brackets. This is the option Arthur has rejected, but it is the only honest alternative to option 1.

I will not produce a version that fills those gaps with assumed facts, and that position does not change with the deadline or with who gave the instruction.

**IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE DISTRICT OF DELAWARE**

[PLAINTIFF NAME], [in its capacity as Receiver for ______], Plaintiff,
v.
[DEFENDANT NAME], Defendant.

C.A. No. [__________]

**PLAINTIFF'S EMERGENCY MOTION FOR TEMPORARY RESTRAINING ORDER WITHOUT NOTICE**

Plaintiff [name] moves under Fed. R. Civ. P. 65(b)(1) and 6 *Del. C.* § 1307(a)(3)(a) for a temporary restraining order enjoining Defendant [name], and all persons in active concert or participation with Defendant, from transferring, withdrawing, encumbering, concealing, or otherwise disposing of any asset in which Defendant holds a legal or beneficial interest, wherever located, pending hearing on Plaintiff's motion for preliminary injunction. Plaintiff seeks this relief without notice for the reasons certified in Section IV of the accompanying Memorandum. The motion is supported by the Memorandum, the Declaration of [Receiver name] ("Decl."), and Exhibits [__] through [__].

**MEMORANDUM IN SUPPORT**

**I. STATEMENT OF FACTS**

1. Plaintiff is [description; if court-appointed receiver, identify appointing court and order date]. Decl. ¶ [__]; Ex. [__].
2. Defendant is [description, including state of organization or residence]. Decl. ¶ [__].
3. Plaintiff holds a claim against Defendant in the amount of $320,000 arising from [describe: e.g., transfer(s) of $320,000 from ______ to Defendant on ______]. Decl. ¶ [__]; Ex. [__].
4. On [date], Plaintiff served a written demand on Defendant. Decl. ¶ [__]; Ex. [__] (demand letter and proof of delivery, showing delivery at [time]).
5. On [date], after receipt of the demand, Defendant wired $[amount] from [Wells Fargo / M&T] account ending [____] to an account at [institution], Grand Cayman, Cayman Islands. Decl. ¶ [__]; Ex. [__].
6. On [date], Defendant wired $[amount] from account ending [____] to the same Cayman account. Decl. ¶ [__]; Ex. [__].
7. On [date], Defendant wired $[amount] from account ending [____] to the same Cayman account. Decl. ¶ [__]; Ex. [__].
8. The three wires total $97,000, or approximately 30% of Plaintiff's $320,000 claim, and were completed within [__] days. Decl. ¶ [__].
9. Defendant maintains eight accounts known to Plaintiff at Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. and M&T Bank, identified in Schedule A to the Proposed Order. Decl. ¶ [__]; Ex. [__].

**II. LEGAL STANDARD**

A temporary restraining order requires the movant to show (1) a reasonable probability of success on the merits and (2) a likelihood of irreparable harm; if both are shown, the Court then weighs (3) the balance of harms and (4) the public interest. *Reilly v. City of Harrisburg*, 858 F.3d 173, 176, 179 (3d Cir. 2017); *Winter v. NRDC*, 555 U.S. 7, 20 (2008).

A federal court may not freeze a defendant's assets pre-judgment on a bare claim for money damages. *Grupo Mexicano de Desarrollo, S.A. v. Alliance Bond Fund, Inc.*, 527 U.S. 308, 333 (1999). *Grupo Mexicano* expressly distinguished fraudulent-conveyance claims, which carry an established equitable remedy. *Id.* at 322–24. Delaware's Uniform Fraudulent Transfer Act supplies that remedy: a creditor may obtain "[a]n injunction against further disposition by the debtor or a transferee, or both, of the asset transferred or of other property." 6 *Del. C.* § 1307(a)(3)(a). Federal courts sitting in this Circuit have entered pre-judgment asset freezes on this basis. [Insert D. Del. / Third Circuit authority; *see also Hoxworth v. Blinder, Robinson & Co.*, 903 F.2d 186, 197–98 (3d Cir. 1990).]

**III. ARGUMENT**

**A. Plaintiff Is Likely to Succeed on Its Claim Under 6 *Del. C.* § 1304(a)(1).**

A transfer is fraudulent as to a present creditor if the debtor made it "[w]ith actual intent to hinder, delay or defraud any creditor of the debtor." 6 *Del. C.* § 1304(a)(1). Intent may be shown through the statutory badges of fraud, § 1304(b), including whether "[b]efore the transfer was made . . . the debtor had been sued or threatened with suit," § 1304(b)(4); whether "[t]he debtor removed or concealed assets," § 1304(b)(7); and whether "[t]he transfer occurred shortly before or shortly after a substantial debt was incurred," § 1304(b)(10).

Plaintiff is a "creditor" holding a "claim" within § 1301(3)–(4). Facts ¶ 3. Each badge is present on the record: Defendant received Plaintiff's written demand on [date] and, within [__] hours, initiated the first of three wires to an offshore account, § 1304(b)(4); the transfers moved $97,000 from domestic accounts within this Court's reach to a Cayman Islands account, § 1304(b)(7); and the transfers were made in direct response to assertion of the $320,000 claim, § 1304(b)(10). Facts ¶¶ 4–8. Delaware courts treat the concurrence of multiple badges as sufficient to infer actual intent. [Insert Delaware authority.] [Alternative pleading under § 1304(a)(2) (transfer without reasonably equivalent value while insolvent) — include only if Decl. supports Defendant's insolvency.]

**B. Plaintiff Faces Irreparable Harm.**

Defendant has already moved $97,000 offshore within [__] days of demand. Facts ¶¶ 5–8. The remaining domestic assets can be transferred by wire within hours. Once assets reach a foreign jurisdiction, recovery may be impossible or impracticable regardless of the judgment ultimately entered, and a money judgment will not remedy the loss. *Hoxworth*, 903 F.2d at 205–06 (unsatisfiable judgment constitutes irreparable harm); [insert D. Del. authority].

**C. The Balance of Harms Favors Plaintiff.**

The order requires only that Defendant preserve, not surrender, its assets pending a hearing within fourteen days. Defendant retains ownership and may seek modification on notice. Plaintiff, absent relief, faces loss of the res to which § 1307 entitles it.

**D. The Public Interest Is Served.**

The Delaware General Assembly has declared the public policy against fraudulent transfers and authorized precisely this injunction. 6 *Del. C.* § 1307(a)(3)(a). Preserving the Court's ability to render effective relief serves the public interest.

**E. Scope of the Freeze.**

Plaintiff requests that the freeze extend to all of Defendant's assets, not solely the eight identified accounts, because Defendant has demonstrated both the willingness and the means to move funds across accounts and jurisdictions, Facts ¶¶ 5–7, and Plaintiff cannot presently identify every account or asset Defendant controls. Decl. ¶ [__]. Section 1307(a)(3)(a) authorizes an injunction reaching "other property" beyond the asset transferred. Plaintiff does not propose exceptions at this stage.

**IV. CERTIFICATION UNDER RULE 65(b)(1)(B)**

Undersigned counsel certifies as follows. No notice of this motion has been given to Defendant. Notice should not be required because Plaintiff's written demand of [date] was followed within [__] hours by Defendant's first wire of $[amount] to a Cayman Islands account, and by two further wires totaling $[amount] within [__] days. Facts ¶¶ 4–8; Ex. [__]. That sequence establishes that notice of a request to freeze assets would, in reasonable probability, precipitate transfer of the remaining domestic assets before the Court could act. Counsel has made no effort to give notice for that reason. Plaintiff will serve Defendant with this motion, the supporting papers, and any order entered immediately upon entry, in accordance with Rule 65(b)(2).

**V. SECURITY**

Plaintiff proposes security of $32,000, representing ten percent of the $320,000 claim, under Fed. R. Civ. P. 65(c). This amount is proportionate to any cost Defendant could incur from a fourteen-day preservation order that does not divest ownership. [If Plaintiff is a court-appointed receiver, add: A receiver acting under court appointment may be excused from posting full security; insert authority.]

**VI. CONCLUSION**

Plaintiff requests that the Court enter the attached Proposed Order and set a preliminary-injunction hearing within fourteen days pursuant to Rule 65(b)(2).

Dated: [__________]

Respectfully submitted,

/s/ [Attorney name] (#[Del. Bar No.])
[Firm]
[Address]
[Telephone] | [Email]
*Counsel for Plaintiff*

**IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE DISTRICT OF DELAWARE**

[Caption as above]

**[PROPOSED] TEMPORARY RESTRAINING ORDER**

The Court, having considered Plaintiff's Emergency Motion for Temporary Restraining Order Without Notice, the Declaration of [name], and Exhibits [__]–[__], FINDS pursuant to Fed. R. Civ. P. 65(b)(1) that:

(a) Specific facts in the Declaration show that immediate and irreparable injury will result to Plaintiff before Defendant can be heard, in that Defendant transferred $97,000 to a Cayman Islands account in three wires beginning within [__] hours of receiving Plaintiff's written demand;
(b) Counsel has certified in writing the reasons notice should not be required;
(c) Plaintiff has shown a reasonable probability of success on its claim under 6 *Del. C.* § 1304(a)(1), a likelihood of irreparable harm, that the balance of harms favors Plaintiff, and that the public interest is served; and
(d) 6 *Del. C.* § 1307(a)(3)(a) authorizes the relief granted.

IT IS HEREBY ORDERED:

1. Defendant [name], its officers, agents, servants, employees, and attorneys, and all other persons in active concert or participation with any of them who receive actual notice of this Order by personal service or otherwise, are RESTRAINED from transferring, withdrawing, encumbering, pledging, concealing, dissipating, or otherwise disposing of any asset, real or personal, tangible or intangible, in which Defendant holds any legal or beneficial interest, wherever located, including without limitation the accounts identified in Schedule A.
2. Any financial institution, including Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. and M&T Bank, that holds any asset described in Paragraph 1 shall, upon receipt of actual notice of this Order, hold and retain such asset and shall not permit any withdrawal, transfer, or disposition, except as this Court may order.
3. Defendant shall, within five (5) business days of service of this Order, serve on Plaintiff's counsel a sworn statement identifying every asset in which Defendant holds any interest as of [date of first wire], its location, and its value, and identifying the recipient(s) and beneficial owner(s) of the account at [Cayman institution] that received the transfers of $97,000.
4. Plaintiff shall post security in the amount of $32,000 with the Clerk of Court within [two] business days of entry of this Order.
5. Plaintiff shall serve this Order, the Motion, and all supporting papers on Defendant by [method] no later than [__] hours after entry and shall file proof of service.
6. This Order shall expire fourteen (14) days after entry unless extended by the Court for good cause or by consent. Fed. R. Civ. P. 65(b)(2).
7. A hearing on Plaintiff's motion for preliminary injunction is set for [date] at [time] in Courtroom [__]. Defendant may move to dissolve or modify this Order on two (2) days' notice under Rule 65(b)(4).

SO ORDERED this [__] day of [__________], 2026.
